http://en.people.cn/n3/2026/0819/c90000-.text: Home Opinion PD Voice Politics Foreign Affairs Business World We Are China Society Culture Sci-Tech Video Photo Sports Travel Military Life Exclusive Specials Languages Chinese Japanese French Spanish Russian Arabic Korean German Portuguese Swahili Italian Kazakh Thai Malay Greek Vietnamese Urdu Hindi Archive Interview: China's growing radio astronomy capacity helps push frontiers of cosmic exploration, Polish astronomer says KRAKOW, Poland, Aug. 18 (Xinhua) -- China's growing radio astronomy capacity, led by the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST), can help scientists tackle some of astronomy's biggest unanswered questions, renowned Polish astronomer Aleksander Wolszczan has said. "FAST has already been playing a really decisive role in investigating properties of pulsars," Wolszczan said in a recent interview with Xinhua. Wolszczan's observations led to the first confirmed discovery of planets outside the solar system more than three decades ago, and he spent years using the Arecibo radio telescope, once regarded as one of the world's best instruments for studying pulsars. After Arecibo ceased operations, FAST has taken over much of that role, he said. "FAST is now the pulsar radio telescope," Wolszczan said, describing it as "bigger, more sensitive" than Arecibo and able to follow a source in the sky for longer. FAST, also known as the "China Sky Eye," has discovered 1,284 pulsars, more than half the combined number discovered by other telescopes worldwide over the same period. Asked what he would study if he had FAST at his disposal, Wolszczan identified three areas: searching for more planets around neutron stars, detecting magnetic fields around planets beyond the solar system, and looking for planets orbiting white dwarfs. The search for magnetic fields around exoplanets is the most compelling of the three, "because that directly relates to life and possibilities for life to exist elsewhere," he said. Scientists have discovered thousands of exoplanets, but have yet to definitively detect a magnetic field around any of them, Wolszczan said. Such fields can help protect planets from harmful particles emitted by their stars and may therefore play an important role in determining whether life can survive. FAST has "a chance to be a very important telescope" in efforts to detect the faint radio signals that could reveal planetary magnetic fields, Wolszczan said, citing its size as a key advantage. He said he will also continue searching for planets orbiting neutron stars to understand why systems like the one he discovered decades ago appear so rare. Wolszczan will also look for planets around white dwarfs, the remnants of stars that have reached the end of their evolution, to answer the question of "how, if at all, planetary systems can survive stellar evolution." The question is also relevant to the solar system's distant future. As stars such as the sun evolve, surrounding planets can be radically transformed or destroyed. Wolszczan described understanding what ultimately happens to such planetary systems as "a very interesting scientific and philosophical question." China is also constructing the QiTai Radio Telescope (QTT), with an aperture of 110 meters, in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. The fully steerable telescope is expected to become the world's largest of its kind when completed in 2028. China's expanding array of technologies is a powerful addition to the broader pool of instruments that scientists worldwide can use to explore unanswered questions, Wolszczan pointed out. "The global community needs China," he said. A Mohu Magyar Péter csütörtök reggeli bejelentésére reagált. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Jake and Callum Robinson’s father Martin gave evidence on Tuesday in the homicide trial, telling the court he doubts he will ever ‘regain my balance’ after the loss. Photograph: Enrique Botello/Reuters View image in fullscreen Jake and Callum Robinson’s father Martin gave evidence on Tuesday in the homicide trial, telling the court he doubts he will ever ‘regain my balance’ after the loss. Photograph: Enrique Botello/Reuters Mexico ‘It’s hell’: father of slain Australian surfers tells Mexico homicide trial about identifying sons’ bodies Three men are on trial over the death of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend, US citizen Jack Carter Rhoad, in Ensenada Agence France-Presse Wed 9 Sep 2026 00.46 EDT Last modified on Wed 9 Sep 2026 00.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court on Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day. Three men are charged in the killing of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, who were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast in April 2024. Authorities say the three were killed in an attempted robbery, and their bodies were found dumped in a cliff-top shaft with gunshot wounds to their heads. ‘I heard a lot of noise’: trial begins in Mexico for alleged killers of Australian surfers and American friend Read more “It’s hell,” the victims’ father Martin Robinson told the court. “It’s hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons.” “It’s not just the loss, but also the potential they had the dreams that lay ahead of them, the places they travelled, and the love they had for others,” he said. Robinson described the ordeal of having to identify his sons’ bodies: Callum by a tattoo on his forearm, while identifying Jake was more difficult and required photographs. Rhoad’s mother Page compared the crime to an execution. “I miss my son every day, and I don’t know if I will ever be able to regain my balance,” she testified. “Carter loved Mexico. He spoke fluent Spanish and loved dancing, Mexican food and its people.” Authorities say the men were killed during an attempt to steal their pickup truck, which was later found burned near their bodies. A protected witness testified Monday that they accompanied one of the defendants to the crime scene and fled after hearing gunshots, and were later threatened into silence. The surfers’ disappearances and deaths sparked widespread outrage and grief in Australia and the United States, prompting a major social media search for their bodies. “We hold no resentment toward the people who did this, but we cannot understand how they could have taken the lives of two beautiful people,” Martin Robinson told the court. The trial is expected to run until the end of September. Rhoad’s widow, Natalie, is scheduled to testify on Wednesday. https://hotnews.ro/victoria-stoiciu-dupa.text: Senatoarea neafiliată Victoria Stoiciu a comentat, marți seară, decizia președintelui Nicușor Dan de a-i interzice accesul la conferințele sale de presă jurnalistului Ovidiu Vanghele. Anunțul a fost făcut chiar de șeful statului la finalul conferinței din cursul serii, de la Cotroceni, atunci când jurnalistul i-a adresat o întrebare. „Nu poți să interzici accesul unui jurnalist, este profund, profund nedemocratic”, a scris senatoarea, într-un mesaj publicat pe pagina ei de Facebook. „Și foarte posibil ilegal, din moment ce legea 544/2001 spune la articolul 19, alin (2) că «Autoritățile și instituțiile publice nu pot interzice în nici un fel accesul mijloacelor de informare în masă la acțiunile publice organizate de acestea», a adăugat Victoria Stoiciu. „«Colegii miloși» au încercat, de fapt, să îl salveze pe președinte de consecințele ordinului său mega (și maga) problematic, nu pe Ovidiu Vanghele. Beneficiarul era președintele”, a comentat senatoarea neafiliată, referindu-se la politica MAGA a președintelui american Donald Trump, a cărui administrație a interzis mai multe publicații de la Casa Albă, decizie inversată de justiția SUA. Articolul 18 din Legea 544/2001, invocată și de Victoria Stoiciu, prevede următoarele la alineatele 3 si 4: Preşedintele Nicuşor Dan l-a anunţat pe jurnalistul Ovidiu Vanghele că nu mai are voie la Palatul Cotroceni, șeful statului arătând că, faţă de injuriile pe care acesta i le-a adus, a dispus să nu mai vină la conferinţele de presă, în timpul acestui mandat. „În primul rând îmi cer scuze că v-am făcut să așteptați. Le-am cerut colegilor mei să nu vă mai permită accesul la conferințele mele pentru injuriile pe care mi le-ați adresat. Colegii mei miloși nu m-au ascultat. Nu veți mai avea acces la Cotroceni în mandatutul meu”, i-a spus Nicușor Dan lui Ovidiu Vanghele. Jurnalistul tocmai îl întrebase pe președinte cum comentează faptul că procurorul general Cristina Chiriac, numită în funcție de președintele Nicușor Dan, a votat „acum o lună, o lună și jumătate în secțiea de procurori a CSM din care face parte, împotriva propunerii ca această secție să sesizeze Inspecția Judiciară, care inspecție să cerceteze o ingerință comisă chiar de dânsa. Este acest lucru parte din reformarea justiției pe care o propuneați cetățenilor români acum un an și jumătate?” „În primul rând, îmi cer scuze pentru că v-am făcut să așteptați atât de mult. În al doilea rând, față de injuriile pe care mi le-ați adus, am dispus ca dumneavoastră să nu mai veniți la conferințe de presă la Palatul Cotroceni în acest mandat. Colegii mei miloși au sărit peste ordinul meu, peste dispoziția mea, v-o comunic eu, dar dumneavoastră nu o să mai veniți și nu o să mai puneți întrebări”, a afirmat apoi președintele Dan. Jurnalistul Ovidiu Vanghele are o experiență de 24 de ani în presă și este autorul mai multor investigații de impact în presa românească. În 2013, el a înființat Centrul pentru Investigații Media (CIM), ONG pe care îl conduce de atunci. Cele mai cunoscute investigații ale sale s-au concentrat pe abuzurile din instituțiile de sănătate mintală și pe fraudele monetare ale statului. A petrecut anul 2016 lucrând împreună cu Ana Poenariu (RISE Project) la serialul „Toți oamenii generalului”, o saga de investigație despre Gabriel Oprea. De asemenea, Ovidiu Vanghele a înființat și a condus echipa editorială a EurActiv România și a colaborat cu Factual (o inițiativă de verificare a faptelor Funky Citizens) și Ziare.com. Din 2017 coordonează proiectul „Să fie Lumină” împreună cu Vlad Stoicescu, cu care a realizat un podcast video săptămânal de actualitate românească. Vanghele este printre autorii seriei de dezvăluiri despre abuzurile sexuale comise de fostul episcop BOR Corneliu Bârlădeanu (Onilă) asupra elevilor de la Seminarul Teologic Ioan Gură de Aur din Huși. O altă serie de investigații realizată de Ovidiu Vanghele alături de jurnalista Bianca Albu a fost „Azilele groazei” urmată de „Toți știau”.
